report.summary: The one failing test, test_deleted_book_disappears[chromium], fails because the books list is served from an in-memory cache that is never invalidated on delete. app/main.py:152 returns the cached list with probability 0.7, so the deleted row is sometimes still rendered. Fix the app first by invalidating `_recent_lists` on add, update and delete, and remove the random cache hit so the outcome is deterministic.

causes.title: Books list randomly served from a stale cache after delete
causes.explanation: list_books() in app/main.py:151-157 returns the cached per-user list whenever the user is in _recent_lists and random.random() < 0.7. Nothing clears that cache when a book is deleted (books_delete at app/main.py:343-350 runs a plain DELETE and never touches _recent_lists) or when one is added. So after the delete redirect, the page is re-rendered from the stale list about 70% of the time and the deleted row still appears. About 30% of the time the DB is re-read and the test passes, so the result depends on chance. The app's stale-data defect is the underlying bug; the nondeterminism is what makes this test flaky rather than consistently failing. The Playwright log matches this: '14 × locator resolved to 1 element', which is one DOM snapshot re-checked, since polling does not re-request the page.
evidence: Actual value: 1 / 14 × locator resolved to 1 element / unexpected value "1"
app/main.py:152: if user_id in _recent_lists and random.random() < 0.7:
app/main.py:343-349: books_delete runs DELETE FROM books without clearing _recent_lists
app/main.py:9: import random (the only use of randomness in the app)
causes.suggested_fix: In the app: remove the random.random() short-circuit in list_books so it always reads the DB, or drop the _recent_lists cache entirely. If a cache is wanted, invalidate _recent_lists[user_id] in insert_book, api_update_book, api_delete_book and books_delete. In the test suite, nothing needs changing; this test is correct. Re-run the test several times after the fix to confirm it passes consistently.
